title: agent-ops installation configuration
description: The shape of config.json: every key an installation may set, its type, its constraints, and — where the code has one — the value used when the key is absent. This file is the machine-readable half of the configuration tables in docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md, docs/REVIEW-PIPELINE-SPEC.md and README.md, which remain the prose authority on what each key means. `default` here records what the code actually falls back to; a key listed in `required` has no fallback anywhere and must be set. Values in this file are the product's, not this installation's: Poetic's own choices live in config.json.

repos.description: The repositories the implementation pipeline works, each with its own ordered work sources. Adding a repository or a source is a config-only change.

sources.description: This repository's work sources, in priority order. The four `issues:<band>` tokens are the same source at four ranks, banded by each issue's Priority field; listing none of them turns issues off for the repository.

implementation_plan_path.description: Path, relative to this repository's root, of its implementation-plan document. Required whenever `sources` lists `implementation-plan` — that source has no path of its own outside this config, and agent-cycle.sh refuses to start without it.

nice.description: Attention bias for the repo walk, after Linux nice: staleness age is multiplied by 1.25^(-nice), so a negative value buys earlier attention and a positive one later. It biases the walk but never starves a repository.

state_dir.description: Where the lock, the shared log and every per-cycle stage transcript live. A leading `~/` is expanded.

workspace_root.description: Where ephemeral clones live and die, including the state repository's mirror. A leading `~/` is expanded.

state_repo.description: Private repository through which `state_dir` replicates between nodes, as `owner/name`. Empty or absent means single-node operation: every mode of scripts/state-sync.sh becomes a no-op and the fleet-flag reads and writes quietly do nothing.

cycles_retained.description: Cycle directories kept in the replicated mirror. Bounds a repository that is force-pushed after every cycle.

state_local_cycles_retained.description: Cycle and review directories the node's own `state_dir` keeps; the same push that replicates prunes to it. Deliberately far above `cycles_retained`, so the local machine is always the longer record.

log_retained_bytes.description: Size at which scripts/rotate-logs.sh rotates dashboard.log, state-sync.log, cron.log and review-cron.log. log.jsonl and review-log.jsonl are never rotated regardless of size.

log_generations.description: Rotated generations of each log kept beside the live file (`<name>.1` … `<name>.<log_generations>`).

coordinator_model.description: The Co-Ordinator's model. Selection is cheap triage.

implementor_model_default.description: The Implementor's model for any change that affects runtime behaviour.

implementor_model_trivial.description: The Implementor's model for docs-, comment- or register-only items.

reviewer_model_default.description: The Reviewer's model for work graded `complexity:low` or `complexity:medium`.

reviewer_model_complex.description: The Reviewer's model for work graded `complexity:high`. Empty falls back to `reviewer_model_default`, which switches the escalation off.

enabler_model.description: The Enabler's model — the highest tier this system runs, affordable only because the eligibility rule engages it rarely. Empty disables the stage.

enabler_assignee.description: GitHub login assigned to every escalation issue the Enabler raises. Required whenever `enabler_model` is set: agent-cycle.sh exits at startup rather than raise an unassigned escalation, since the assignment is what stops the pipeline selecting its own SOS as work.

enabler_after_coordinator_cycles.description: How many distinct cycles that ran a Co-Ordinator to completion must follow a block before the item becomes Enabler-eligible. Counted in cycles rather than hours because a fleet stood down on a usage limit has not 'had a chance' at anything.

refinement_after_coordinator_cycles.description: The same threshold for a block whose kind is `needs-refinement`. Absent, it inherits `enabler_after_coordinator_cycles`.

enabler_recheck_hours.description: How long after an examination the Enabler may examine the same item again. 0 disables re-examination.

enabler_escalation_label.description: Applied to every issue the Enabler raises, for the human's filter and for its own duplicate guard. Must not be `blocked`, which excludes an issue from the `issues` source.

needs_refinement_label.description: Projected onto an issue-type item while its refinement block is open, and the label a human applies by hand to flag one themselves. Empty disables both directions. Must not be `blocked`.

refinement_max_per_engagement.description: How many refinement-class items one Enabler engagement takes on; ordinary blocked items are uncapped and are never displaced by them. 0 removes the class from engagements while still recording the blocks.

unvoid_label.description: The label a human applies on GitHub to ask for a void to be reopened. No stage ever applies it, so 'only a human may clear a void' is unchanged; what it gives them is a way to say so from where they are.

prompt_overrides.description: Per-installation prompt extension or replacement, so house rules survive an update instead of forking prompts/. A relative path resolves against `state_dir`. Absent, or a stage absent from it, reproduces the shipped prompt byte for byte.

pr_label.description: Applied to every pull request the implementation pipeline raises, and the label by which every gatherer, and the back-pressure limit, finds them again. It must not be empty: `gh pr list --label ''` matches every open pull request, so an empty value would hand the pipeline other people's work as its own.

branch_prefix.description: Branch naming for the implementation pipeline: `<branch_prefix><item-slug>`. Branches outside it belong to humans — the Human Gate reads this to tell ours from theirs, so it must not be empty.

max_open_agent_prs.description: Back-pressure: total open pull requests (draft or ready) carrying `pr_label` across all repositories, plus live claim-registry entries.

candidates_max.description: How many ranked candidates the Co-Ordinator returns; the Script claims down the list, so a lost race costs the next-best item rather than the cycle.

claim_ttl_hours.description: Age beyond which lib/claim.sh sweeps a claim-registry entry. Set it far beyond a whole cycle, so only a dead node's claim ever expires.

abandoned_draft_after_hours.description: How long a draft pull request this system raised may sit without real activity before it counts as abandoned and finishing it becomes selectable work. Beyond a whole cycle, so a draft merely being worked never qualifies.

crash_loop_after.description: Consecutive same-detail Co-Ordinator failures, fleet-wide with no intervening success, before the Script escalates the crash loop as an issue. 0 disables the check.

crash_loop_repo.description: Where the crash-loop escalation issue is filed, as `owner/name` — the pipeline's own repository, because a Co-Ordinator that cannot run belongs to no target repo's backlog. Empty disables the check.

timeout_coordinator.description: Per-stage wall-clock timeout for the Co-Ordinator, in minutes.

timeout_implementor.description: Per-stage wall-clock timeout for the Implementor, in minutes.

timeout_reviewer.description: Per-stage wall-clock timeout for the Reviewer, in minutes.

timeout_enabler.description: Per-stage wall-clock timeout for the Enabler, in minutes.

lock_stale_after.description: Hours after which a held cycle lock is treated as stale, killed, and warned about. Must exceed the sum of the stage timeouts plus slack.

limit_cooldown_default.description: Hours to stand down after an ordinary usage-limit error whose reset time cannot be parsed.

disable_default_ttl.description: Hours `--disable` lasts when `--for` does not say. Long enough to cover an editing session, short enough that a forgotten switch costs a few cycles rather than every future one.

none_selected_recheck_hours.description: The no-op short-circuit's safety valve: the Co-Ordinator is engaged regardless once the last `none-selected` is this old, even if nothing changed. 0 disables the valve — don't.

image_behind_grace_hours.description: How long a node may sit behind the registry's newest image before the dashboard badge turns amber and scripts/check-node-image.sh fails. A roll defers while a cycle is in flight, so being behind a more recent image than this is the ordinary mid-roll state, not a fault.

dashboard_refresh_seconds.description: How often an open dashboard tab reloads to pick up freshly-written data. Match it to the heartbeat cadence.

schedule.description: The cadence of every cron line a containerised node installs, rendered by deploy/docker/render-crontab.sh. Absent, every field below takes its default.

cycle_hours.description: The hour field of the implementation cycle's crontab line; `*` is every hour.

excluded_minutes.description: Minutes the per-node cycle minute (env or hash) may never land on. A deployment with no conflicting workload ships []. Excluding every minute of the hour is a misconfiguration the renderer refuses rather than spinning on.

excluded_minutes_reason.description: Free text recording why `excluded_minutes` excludes what it does. Read by nothing; kept for the next reader.

review_hour.description: The hour the review tick fires.

review_offset_minutes.description: Minutes past the node's cycle minute (mod 60) the review tick's minute is set to, keeping one node's two heavy pipelines apart within the hour.

heartbeat_minutes.description: Interval, in minutes, of the dashboard heartbeat cron line.

log_rotation_minute.description: The minute past every hour scripts/rotate-logs.sh runs.

review.description: The project-review pipeline's tunables. Absent, the implementation pipeline runs exactly as it does now and review-cycle.sh has nothing to run.

repos.description: The repositories to review — a plain list of slugs, since a review has no per-repo work-source structure.

model.description: The Reviewer-Agent's model — the lead that drives the skill, which delegates well-scoped sub-tasks to lower-cost subagents of its own.

pr_label.description: Applied to every review pull request. Keep it distinct from the implementation pipeline's `pr_label`, so review PRs never count against `max_open_agent_prs`. It must not be empty, for the reason given there.

branch_prefix.description: Branch naming for the review pipeline: `<branch_prefix><date>`. A branch is already scoped to its repository, so no slug is needed.

timeout_review.description: Per-repo wall-clock timeout for the Reviewer-Agent, in minutes. A full review is long; be generous.

lock_stale_after.description: Hours after which a held review lock is treated as stale. Larger than the implementation pipeline's, because two full reviews back-to-back can exceed it.

min_days_between_reviews.description: The skip-guard threshold: a repository reviewed within this many days is skipped. Leave a day of slack against the intended cadence, so a review that lands late one week is not pushed a full extra week the next.

not_before.description: Optional timestamp before which no review may start — every repository, not one. Absent or empty means no stand-down. It expires by itself, which is why it exists rather than raising `min_days_between_reviews`: a threshold has to be put back by hand, and a cadence left quietly throttled is not noticed for weeks.

modelId.description: A model identifier: either bare (`claude-sonnet-5`) or provider-qualified (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`). Anthropic is the only executable provider today, so the two forms are the same value; a qualifier naming any other provider is rejected at cycle start.

modelIdOrEmpty.description: A model identifier as in `modelId`, or empty to switch the stage that reads it off.

label.description: A GitHub label name. Empty, where a key allows it, switches that labelling off.

timeoutMinutes.description: A per-stage wall-clock timeout, in whole minutes.

promptOverride.description: One stage's override. `extend` appends fragments to the shipped prompt in the order listed; `replace` substitutes a file for prompts/<stage>.md itself, which stops that stage receiving this product's future updates.
